typical_rounds: Round 1: Online Assessment (Quantitative Aptitude, Logical Reasoning & Foundational Coding)
Round 2: Technical Interview 1 (Data Structures, Algorithms & Core Computer Science)
Round 3: Technical Interview 2 (System Architecture, Tech Stack & Resume Project Deep-Dive)
Round 4: HR & Behavioral Round (Cultural Fit, Situational Questions & Career Goals)
commonly_tested_topics: Data Structures (Arrays, Strings, Linked Lists, Trees, Graphs, HashMaps)
Object-Oriented Programming (Inheritance, Polymorphism, Encapsulation, Abstraction)
Database Management Systems & SQL Queries (Joins, Indexing, Transactions)
Operating Systems & Computer Networks (Threads, Deadlocks, TCP/IP, HTTP/S)
Resume Project Architecture & Problem-Solving Trade-offs
STAR Method Scenarios (Conflict Resolution, Team Leadership, Adaptability)
preparation_tips: Clarify constraints, edge cases, and assumptions before writing any code.
Analyze and state time and space complexity for both brute-force and optimized solutions.
Thoroughly review every project, library, and metric stated on your resume.
Structure behavioral responses using the Situation, Task, Action, Result (STAR) framework.
Prepare 2-3 thoughtful questions for the interviewers about engineering culture and tech stack.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Online Coding Assessment (Google Online Challenge on HackerEarth)
Round 2: Technical Phone Screen (Algorithms & Data Structures via Google Docs/Meet)
Round 3: Onsite / Virtual Technical Interview 1 (Advanced DSA & Graph/DP Algorithms)
Round 4: Onsite / Virtual Technical Interview 2 (Data Structures, Trees & Optimization)
Round 5: Googleyness & Leadership (Navigating Ambiguity, Teamwork & Behavioral)
commonly_tested_topics: Graphs (BFS/DFS, Dijkstra, Topological Sort, Union-Find)
Dynamic Programming (1D/2D, Memoization & Tabulation)
Binary Trees, BST, Heaps & Segment Trees / Tries
Recursion, Backtracking & Two Pointers
Time & Space Complexity Proofs
Googleyness (Intellectual Humility, Navigating Ambiguity, Collaborative Problem-Solving)
preparation_tips: Practice coding in plain text editors without syntax highlighting or auto-complete.
Think aloud continuously — Google interviewers heavily evaluate your reasoning process.
Always verify your solution against boundary conditions, empty inputs, and large inputs before claiming it works.
For Googleyness, emphasize proactive initiative, teamwork, constructive feedback, and ethical decision-making.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Online Assessment (OA 1: Code Debugging & Coding; OA 2: Work Simulation & Work Styles)
Round 2: Technical Interview 1 (Algorithms, Data Structures & Leadership Principles)
Round 3: Technical Interview 2 (Low-Level Design / OOP & Leadership Principles)
Round 4: Bar Raiser Round (In-depth Behavioral + Scalability/Coding by an Independent Evaluator)
commonly_tested_topics: Binary Trees, Binary Search Trees & Heaps
Arrays, Strings, Sliding Window & HashMaps
Graphs & Breadth-First / Depth-First Search
Object-Oriented Design (Clean Code, SOLID Principles)
16 Amazon Leadership Principles (Customer Obsession, Ownership, Bias for Action, Dive Deep)
preparation_tips: Every single interview round includes 15-20 minutes dedicated to Amazon Leadership Principles.
Prepare at least two distinct real-world stories for every major Leadership Principle using the STAR method.
Always justify customer-centric thinking and trade-offs in design and architectural questions.
Write modular, clean code with descriptive variable and function names.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Online Coding Assessment (Codility platform, 3 coding problems)
Round 2: Technical Interview 1 (Data Structures, Algorithms & Code Optimization)
Round 3: Technical Interview 2 (Systems Fundamentals, Multithreading & DSA)
Round 4: Technical & Cultural Fit / Partner Director Round (Design, Core CS & Microsoft Values)
commonly_tested_topics: Linked Lists, Trees (Tree Traversals, Lowest Common Ancestor) & Graphs
Strings, Palindromes & Matrix Manipulations
Dynamic Programming & Greedy Algorithms
Operating Systems (Process synchronization, Memory management, Paging)
Database Fundamentals & SQL Queries
Growth Mindset & Inclusive Collaboration
preparation_tips: Microsoft interviewers place heavy emphasis on testing your code on edge cases and debugging.
Demonstrate a growth mindset: be receptive to interviewer hints and iterate on your solutions.
Revise OS and multithreading concepts thoroughly for circuital/software engineer tracks.
Be prepared to write syntactically correct code and step through each line manually.

typical_rounds: Round 1: TCS NQT (National Qualifier Test: Foundation Section + Advanced Cognitive & Coding)
Round 2: Technical Interview (Core Engineering Concepts, DSA, Resume Projects & Languages)
Round 3: Managerial Interview (Problem Solving, Project Scenarios & Real-Time Challenges)
Round 4: HR Interview (Willingness to Relocate, Shifts, Background & Communication)
commonly_tested_topics: Quantitative Aptitude, Logical Reasoning & Verbal Ability
C, C++, Java, or Python Basics (Pointers, Memory, OOP)
Database Concepts, Normalization & Basic SQL Queries
Data Structures (Arrays, Stacks, Queues, Searching & Sorting)
Academic Projects and Final-Year Project Implementation
preparation_tips: Speed and accuracy in the Foundation Cognitive Section of TCS NQT determine Digital vs Prime vs Ninja qualification.
Be completely transparent about your resume projects — interviewers drill down on individual contributions.
Maintain a polite, confident, and professional demeanor throughout the managerial and HR rounds.
Practice explaining standard algorithms (Binary Search, Bubble/Merge Sort) and writing their code on paper.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Infosys Online Test / InfyTQ / HackWithInfy (Reasoning, Verbal & Coding)
Round 2: Technical Interview (DSA, OOP, Web Technologies & Resume Verification)
Round 3: HR Interview (Career Aspirations, Relocation Flexibility & Communication Skills)
commonly_tested_topics: Object-Oriented Programming (Java/Python OOP paradigms)
Basic Data Structures (Arrays, Strings, Stacks, Queues)
SQL Queries, Joins, Primary/Foreign Keys & ACID Properties
Software Engineering Methodologies (Agile, SDLC phases)
Web Basics (HTML, CSS, REST APIs, HTTP methods)
preparation_tips: Prepare strong foundational knowledge in at least one object-oriented language (preferably Java or Python).
Practice SQL queries on employee/department schemas (finding Nth highest salary, grouping, joins).
Be ready to explain the architecture and technology choices behind your college projects.
Show genuine enthusiasm for continuous learning and readiness to adapt to new technology domains.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Cognitive & Technical Assessment (English, Critical Thinking, Abstract Reasoning, MS Office & Cloud basics)
Round 2: Coding Assessment (2 coding questions in 45 minutes)
Round 3: Communication Assessment (Automated AI-based spoken English test: reading, repetition, storytelling)
Round 4: Technical + HR Interview (Combined interview evaluating projects, situational judgment & soft skills)
commonly_tested_topics: Pseudo-code Interpretation & Output Prediction
Cloud & Digital Fundamentals (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, Cyber basics)
Basic Networking Fundamentals (IP addressing, DNS, Firewalls)
Fundamental Coding (String reversals, Palindromes, Array sorting)
Situational Judgment & Client-Facing Behavioral Scenarios
preparation_tips: Practice solving pseudo-code snippets quickly under timed conditions.
For the automated Communication Assessment, speak clearly at a measured pace into a good headset.
Prepare a concise chronological walkthrough of your resume projects emphasizing your individual role.
Demonstrate customer-first thinking and adaptability to work across hybrid environments.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Technical & Cognitive Assessment (Pseudo-code, English Communication, Game-based Aptitude)
Round 2: Spoken English / Communication Assessment
Round 3: Technical Interview (Programming fundamentals, DBMS, Project discussion)
Round 4: HR Interview (Behavioral questions, Willingness to relocate & Shift flexibility)
commonly_tested_topics: Game-based Cognitive Aptitude (Memory, Spatial Reasoning, Speed)
Pseudo-code logic and bitwise operations
Core Java / C++ Fundamentals and OOP concepts
Database Management Systems & SQL syntax
Academic Project Lifecycle & Technology Stack
preparation_tips: Familiarize yourself with game-based aptitude challenges beforehand to avoid surprise during Round 1.
Revise data types, operator precedence, and loop execution in pseudo-codes.
Ensure you can write clean code for basic string and array operations on a shared screen.
Exhibit clear communication, professional etiquette, and flexibility in the HR discussion.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Online Assessment (HackerRank: Algorithmic Coding + Aptitude + CS Fundamentals)
Round 2: Technical Interview 1 (Advanced Data Structures, Trees, Graphs & Dynamic Programming)
Round 3: Technical Interview 2 (System Design / Low-Level Design & Operating Systems)
Round 4: Engineering Director / HR Round (Innovation, Values Alignment & Behavioral)
commonly_tested_topics: Binary Trees, BST, Tries & Segment Trees
Dynamic Programming (Matrix DP, Subsets, Strings)
Graph Traversals (BFS/DFS, Topological Sort, Shortest Path)
Operating Systems (Virtual Memory, Semaphores, Multithreading, Concurrency)
Object-Oriented Design & Design Patterns (Factory, Observer, Singleton)
preparation_tips: Master tree and graph algorithms along with dynamic programming patterns.
Be prepared to write bug-free code and mathematically justify time and space complexity.
Deeply understand systems concepts like memory management, caching, and thread synchronization.
Align your answers with Adobe core values: Genuine, Exceptional, Innovative, and Involved.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Elite NTH Assessment (Aptitude, Written Communication Essay & Coding)
Round 2: Technical Interview (Core CS, Programming languages & Resume Projects)
Round 3: HR Interview (Behavioral, Background verification & Career orientation)
commonly_tested_topics: Numerical Ability, Logical Reasoning & English Essay Writing
Programming Fundamentals in C, C++, Java or Python
Data Structures (Arrays, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues)
Relational Databases, Keys, Constraints & SQL Queries
Final Year Project Architecture and Problem Statement
preparation_tips: Focus on grammar, structure, and clarity in the Written Communication essay section.
Practice basic algorithmic coding problems (Fibonacci, Factorial, Matrix operations, Prime checks).
Be ready to explain how your project solves a genuine practical problem.
Maintain high confidence and clear spoken communication in both Technical and HR rounds.

typical_rounds: Round 1: GenC / GenC Next Assessment (Aptitude, Domain MCQs & Coding Challenges)
Round 2: Technical Interview (DSA, OOP, SQL & Web/Cloud Technologies)
Round 3: HR Interview (Cultural Alignment, Communication & Willingness to Relocate)
commonly_tested_topics: Analytical & Quantitative Reasoning
Object-Oriented Programming (Java/Python/C++)
Database Queries (SELECT, GROUP BY, HAVING, Subqueries)
Data Structures & Basic Search/Sort Algorithms
Resume Projects & Tech Stack Components
preparation_tips: For GenC Next, master medium-level DSA problems in arrays, strings, and hash maps.
Review core database concepts including normalization forms, primary keys, and index types.
Walk the interviewer through your project's architecture, tools used, and personal contributions.
Express a proactive attitude toward learning emerging tech stacks like cloud and AI.

typical_rounds: Round 1: Technical Screening (2 algorithmic coding problems in 45 minutes on CoderPad)
Round 2: Onsite Technical Coding 1 (Data Structures, Algorithms & Edge Cases)
Round 3: Onsite Technical Coding 2 (Problem Solving, Optimization & Complexity)
Round 4: Behavioral & Engineering Culture (Collaboration, Conflict, Meta Values)
commonly_tested_topics: Binary Trees, Graph Traversals & Binary Search Variations
Sliding Window, Two Pointers & HashMaps
Dynamic Programming & Heap / Priority Queues
Time & Space Complexity Optimization
Meta Core Values (Move Fast, Focus on Long-Term Impact, Be Direct)
preparation_tips: Pacing is critical: you must solve 2 coding questions cleanly within 45 minutes.
Communicate before coding, test code thoroughly with dry-runs, and minimize bug density.
Be prepared to write code on a blank board/CoderPad without compilation or debugger assistance.
Prepare concrete stories illustrating how you resolved technical disagreements and prioritized impact.
